about.title: Palm Springs Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Palm Springs residents rely on a mix of local clinics, urgent care centers, and hospitals that also serve visitors drawn to the desert each year, and that steady patient volume means errors can and do happen. Medical malpractice covers situations where a provider's care fell below the accepted standard and caused real harm — not simply a treatment that didn't work out as hoped. Because Riverside County has both large hospital systems and smaller specialty practices, malpractice claims here can involve emergency rooms, surgical centers, or long-term care facilities. California's MICRA law puts specific rules around these cases, including notice requirements and expert review, so timing and documentation matter from the start. LawProactive doesn't practice law or take a fee itself; we simply connect you with an independent attorney who can evaluate what happened, explain whether MICRA's rules apply to your situation, and help you understand realistic next steps without any upfront cost.

whyChoose.title: Why Get Guidance Before You Wait

items.title: Strict, Layered Deadlines
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from discovering the harm, and never more than three years from the injury itself, to bring a claim. An attorney can help track which clock applies to your situation.

items.title: 90-Day Notice Requirement
items.desc: Before filing suit, California law typically requires sending the provider a 90-day notice of intent. Missing this step or handling it incorrectly can delay or jeopardize a claim.

items.title: Expert Review Is Usually Required
items.desc: Because a bad medical outcome alone isn't proof of malpractice, a qualified medical expert almost always needs to review the case. An independent attorney can help arrange that evaluation early.

items.question: Is every bad outcome from a Palm Springs hospital visit considered malpractice?
items.answer: No. California law requires showing the provider's care fell below an accepted medical standard and that this caused your harm. A poor result alone, even a serious one, isn't automatically malpractice — an independent attorney can help assess whether the facts support a claim.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a medical malpractice claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have one year from when you discovered (or reasonably should have discovered) the injury, but no more than three years from the date of the injury itself. There are limited exceptions, so getting an early evaluation matters.

items.question: Are damages capped in California medical malpractice cases?
items.answer: Yes, California places a statutory cap on non-economic damages (like pain and suffering) under MICRA, and that cap rises annually. Economic damages, such as medical bills and lost income, are generally not subject to this same cap.

items.question: Does LawProactive handle malpractice claims directly?
items.answer: No, LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm. We help match Palm Springs residents with an independent attorney who can review the details of their care and explain options, at no upfront cost.
